answer: Randomness-locked admission slots. Each epoch, a verifiable random beacon draws a plume of candidate slots; an agent must commit a registration whose hash lands in that draw's narrow kernel to activate. Because the beacon is unbounded until broadcast, attackers cannot pre-mine matching identities. Every failed attempt consumes a full registration thread, so N sybils cost N independent commitments per epoch, and the hit rate stays proportional to the published tolerance τ, making mass registration linearly expensive.
